utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm glad you came in. Burning can be caused by a urine infection, but I'll check for other causes so we choose the right treatment. Can you tell me more about your symptoms since yesterday?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago, and it really stings and burns worst right at the end. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out so I have to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I have not seen any blood.

Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: Have you had any fever, chills, pain in your back or sides, nausea or vomiting? Any pain low in your tummy, or difficulty getting urine out?
reply: I have not had any fevers or shivers and feel fine apart from this, there is nothing in my back, I am eating normally and have not been sick, and I just have that low ache above my bladder with no difficulty getting urine out.

Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

utterance: I ask everyone these questions confidentially because some sexually transmitted infections can also cause burning. Have you had a new sexual partner recently, and do you use condoms? Have you or a partner ever had a sexually transmitted infection or had a recent test?
reply: I have a boyfriend and we have been together about a year with just him, and we do not use condoms because I am on the pill.

utterance: Have either of you had a sexually transmitted infection before, or been tested? Have you missed any pills recently?
reply: No, that has never been a problem, and I am on the pill and do not miss it.

utterance: Tell me about your previous urine infections: how often have they happened, when was the last one, and were urine samples tested? Which antibiotics helped, and have you taken any antibiotics recently?
reply: I had one urinary tract infection about two years ago and that is it, and I have not had any antibiotics this year.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months

utterance: Do you remember which antibiotic you took then or whether the urine test showed any resistant germs? Do you have any kidney problems, kidney stones, diabetes or problems with your immune system?
reply: I do not remember the antibiotic from back then, and I do not have any kidney problems, diabetes, or issues with my immune system.

utterance: Are you taking anything besides the pill, including pharmacy remedies for this? Any medicine allergies or reactions?
reply: I am just on the combined oral contraceptive pill, I am not taking any pharmacy remedies for this, and I am not allergic to anything that I know of.

utterance: Your symptoms sound most like a bladder infection. With your permission, I'll check your temperature and pulse, feel your tummy and gently check over the kidneys in your back. We can check a urine sample too; an internal examination doesn't appear necessary.
reply: Okay, if that is what we need to do. Can I just get the script afterwards so I can get back to work?

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: Yes, we can treat this today. Your examination is reassuring and the urine check supports a bladder infection, without signs of a kidney infection. Although pregnancy sounds very unlikely, is it okay to check a pregnancy test on the urine before choosing treatment? We also routinely offer chlamydia screening to sexually active people under 30, even without symptoms; would you like that today?
reply: Do we really need a pregnancy test? I am just really keen to get my script so I can get back to my shift at the café.

utterance: No, it isn't essential given your normal recent period and reliable pill use, so we can skip it. The sexual health screen is optional too and can be arranged another time. I'll prescribe a short course for the bladder infection now.
reply: Oh, thank you, that is a relief. Can I just grab the prescription from you now so I can head straight back to work?

utterance: One last medicine safety check: have you ever been told you have G6PD deficiency, an inherited condition where certain medicines can damage your red blood cells?
reply: I have never heard of that, so I do not think so.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Your prescription is for nitrofurantoin: one 100 mg capsule four times a day with food for five days. Finish the course. It may cause nausea or turn urine darker yellow or brown; that colour change is harmless. If you develop a rash, stop it and seek advice; breathing trouble or facial swelling means call 000. It doesn't directly affect your pill, but vomiting or severe diarrhoea can—follow your pill's sick-day instructions and use condoms if that happens.

For discomfort, you can take paracetamol 500–1000 mg every 4–6 hours if needed, no more than 4000 mg in 24 hours. Drink enough to stay hydrated, without forcing extra water, and don't hold your urine. Avoid urinary alkalinising sachets such as Ural while on this antibiotic, as they can reduce its effect.

You should start feeling better within 48 hours. If you aren't improving by then, or symptoms return after treatment, come back so we can send urine to the lab and reassess. A lab culture isn't routinely needed for a straightforward infection like this. Seek urgent care the same day if you develop fever, shaking chills, back or side pain, vomiting, or feel very unwell—these can mean infection has reached the kidneys. You're okay to return to work if you feel able, with access to drinks and toilet breaks. Is there anything about the treatment you'd like clarified?
reply: No, that all makes sense, thank you. I am just really glad to finally get this sorted and get back to my shift.
